questions.stem: A pipeline must start whenever a new file lands in a storage folder. What do you set up?

options.text: A deployment rule on the storage account folder
A schedule that runs every minute
A storage event trigger for the pipeline
A Git webhook on the workspace's repository

questions.explanation: Event-based triggers start a pipeline when events such as a file being created occur, so it runs as soon as the file arrives instead of polling.

questions.stem: The event trigger from the previous design must fire only for .csv files in one folder. What do you configure?

options.text: Nothing; event triggers can't filter, so they fire for every file in the storage account
An event filter on the Subject field that matches the folder name and the .csv file type
A ForEach activity in the pipeline that skips every file not ending in .csv
A second pipeline that deletes other files before the trigger fires

questions.explanation: Event triggers can filter events by folder name, file name, file type and container through the Subject field, so only matching files start the pipeline.

questions.stem: Where do you set a pipeline to run every day at 02:00?

options.text: In the Git panel of the workspace
In the pipeline's schedule settings
In the default lakehouse's settings
In the capacity settings

questions.explanation: Each pipeline has a schedule with a frequency, start time and time zone.

questions.stem: Which three can start a pipeline run? Each correct answer is a complete solution.

options.text: Opening the lakehouse it writes to
Running it on demand
Adding a sensitivity label
A schedule
An event trigger, such as a file arriving in storage

questions.explanation: A pipeline runs on demand, on a schedule, or when an event trigger fires. Labels and opening items don't start runs.

questions.stem: A pipeline must run at 06:00 every weekday and also every hour on Saturdays. What do you set up?

options.text: Two pipelines with one schedule each
Two schedules on the same pipeline
An event trigger with a time filter
One schedule every hour, with an If Condition to skip weekday hours

questions.explanation: A pipeline can have up to 20 schedules, each with its own frequency and start and end times.

questions.stem: You schedule a pipeline that must keep running daily for years. The schedule asks for an end date. What do you do?

options.text: Leave the end date empty for an open-ended schedule
Set the end date far in the future, such as 01/01/2099
Use an event trigger instead
Re-create the schedule every month

questions.explanation: Schedules need both a start and end date. To run long-term, set the end date far in the future.

questions.stem: You set email notifications for pipeline failures. A developer runs the pipeline on demand and it fails, but no email arrives. Why?

options.text: Notifications are sent only after three failures
Notifications are sent only for failed scheduled runs
Notifications go only to workspace Admins
Notifications need an event trigger

questions.explanation: Failure notifications apply to scheduled runs. On-demand runs don't send them.

questions.stem: A pipeline started by a storage event trigger uses @pipeline().TriggerEvent.FileName. When you test it manually, the expression fails. Which expression handles this?

options.text: @pipeline().parameters.FileName
@pipeline()?.TriggerEvent?.FileName
@@pipeline().TriggerEvent.FileName
@trigger().outputs.body.fileName

questions.explanation: During manual tests the trigger's file and folder parameters aren't set and return NULL. The ? operator handles the NULL values.

questions.stem: A schedule passes a value for a parameter named region, but the pipeline defines the parameter as Region. What happens at run time?

options.text: The value is matched without regard to case
The schedule is disabled
The pipeline fails before it starts
The mismatched parameter is ignored

questions.explanation: Schedule parameter names must exactly match the pipeline's parameter names. Mismatched names are ignored at run time.

questions.stem: Put the steps to create a storage event trigger from a pipeline's canvas in order.

options.text: In the Set alert panel, choose the source, such as OneLake events or Azure Blob events
Choose the event types and filter them with the Subject field
Choose the workspace to store the trigger and name it as a Reflex item
Select Trigger on the Home ribbon of the pipeline canvas
Select Create

questions.explanation: You open the trigger from the canvas, pick the event source, narrow the events, choose where the Reflex item is stored, and create it.
